note: Tuesday 07:02 SGT run — BEFORE Asia's open (SGX 09:00, HKEX 09:30) and the US Tuesday open, framed against the Mon 3 Aug US close (the first live session since Sunday's pre-open run). THE PIVOT this run: the Iran/Hormuz front DE-ESCALATED — President Trump called off the 'massive' strikes he had threatened for the weekend and said talks to wind down the war began Monday afternoon, with a deal to reopen the Strait of Hormuz described as 'imminent' (Iran confirms talks with mediators). Oil crashed ~5-7% (WTI from ~$86 toward ~$79-82) and US equities ripped to records — S&P 500 +1.48% to 7,600.50, Nasdaq +2.1% to 25,913.9, Dow a record 53,178.41 (+1.32%), VIX ~16. Metals held their bid anyway (silver opened ~$58.3-58.6, gold recovered above ~$4,050) — the structural bull, not just the war premium. Other fresh threads: a KOSPI rout on record foreign selling (weekend), the Hang Seng's best week since Sep-2025 on a 'moderately loose' Politburo pledge, Xiaomi +7.7% on new EV models, and Singtel/KKR's >US$3.9B ST Telemedia data-centre deal. 6 of 14 items are dated 1-3 Aug. Note: the sharp July-payroll deceleration theme (~73k whisper + big May/Jun downward revisions circulating) is NOT published as fact — the official July jobs report is due Fri 7 Aug; it is listed as the key catalyst to watch, not a released print. Every item source-verified; nothing published with a guessed figure.

items.headline: Trump calls off 'massive' Iran strikes, talks begin Monday; Hormuz reopening 'imminent' — oil crashes, stocks surge to records
items.summary: The Iran/Hormuz war front de-escalated sharply: President Trump said he held off on the massive strikes he had threatened for the weekend and that talks to wind down the conflict began Monday afternoon, with a deal to reopen the Strait of Hormuz — through which ~a fifth of traded oil and gas passes — described as 'imminent' (Iran confirmed it is in talks with mediators). Crude fell ~5-7% intraday (WTI from ~$86 toward ~$79-82; Brent lower) and US equities ripped to records: the S&P 500 rose 1.48% to 7,600.50, the Nasdaq 2.1% to 25,913.9 and the Dow a record 53,178.41 (+1.32%), with the VIX around 16.
items.actionable: The de-escalation unwinds the oil/inflation premium that had pressured the rate-sensitive book (levered silver, S-REITs, HK tech) and lifts broad risk — a relief for the tech-beta and SGX/HK sleeves, but a headwind for the small energy long (USO/XLE) and a partial safe-haven unwind for gold/silver. Watch whether the Hormuz deal is actually signed when oil reopens and Asia trades; a talks collapse snaps the oil/safe-haven bid straight back, so keep gold-heavy GDX as the two-way hedge rather than chasing the risk-on tape.

items.headline: US stocks rip to records: S&P +1.48% to 7,600.50, Nasdaq +2.1%, Dow a record 53,178.41
items.summary: Wall Street rallied broadly on the Iran de-escalation and falling oil: the S&P 500 gained 1.48% to a record 7,600.50, the Nasdaq Composite jumped 2.1% to 25,913.9 (mega-cap/hyperscaler led, Amazon at a record after its AWS blowout) and the Dow rose 693 points (+1.32%) to an all-time-high 53,178.41. The VIX slid further to ~16. The move extended the two-day relief rally that had reversed the late-July hawkish-FOMC selloff, leaving all three indices at or near records with breadth broad (~70%+ of the S&P above its 200-DMA).
items.actionable: A clean risk-on session with broad breadth is a positive read-through to the tech-beta parts of the book (SMIC chip leg, HK tech). But the S&P at a fresh record with the 10Y still ~4.7% and inflation sticky at 3.3% leaves little valuation cushion, and the rally leans on Iran-deal optimism that is not yet signed. Don't chase the record; keep the USD cash pile as dry powder and let this week's SGX/HK earnings and Friday's July jobs report confirm the turn before redeploying.

items.headline: Silver opens higher ~$58.3-58.6 and gold recovers above ~$4,050 even as risk-on returns and oil falls
items.summary: Precious metals held their bid despite the safe-haven-unwinding Iran de-escalation: silver opened higher near $58.3-58.6/oz (recovering Friday's ~$57.7 hot-PCE dip) and gold climbed back above ~$4,050/oz, with December gold futures around $4,135. The resilience — metals firming while oil fell and equities rallied — points to the structural bull (the Silver Institute's 6th straight annual deficit; a record year of gold-fund inflows) rather than a pure fear bid. Physical metals and the miners (GDX/SILJ/SLVP/SLV) carried Monday's US-session strength into the Asia open.
items.actionable: The book's single most important line item — levered silver plus the miners — showed its structural resilience: it firmed even as the war premium bled out and the dollar stayed firm, the constructive tell. The two-sided risk remains a hotter Fed path (10Y ~4.7%), but with oil de-escalating and labor softening the near-term balance tilts back toward the metals. Favor gold-heavy GDX over pure silver leverage until Friday's jobs report clarifies the rate path.

items.headline: KOSPI rout deepens on record foreign selling; EM-Asia tech sentiment fragile
items.summary: South Korea's KOSPI extended a sharp selloff into the weekend as foreign investors dumped Korean stocks at near-crisis scale — roughly ₩28trn of net selling across an eight-session stretch, one of the heaviest foreign-outflow runs on record — with retail anger flaring over leveraged-ETF losses on SK Hynix/Samsung AI names. The rout is a caution flag on fragile EM-Asia tech risk appetite even as Hong Kong rallied, and a reminder that the AI-hardware trade remains two-sided after the late-July >$1trn semis round-trip.
items.actionable: A sympathy caution for the SMIC (0981) chip leg and the broader EM-Asia tech beta in the book: foreign capitulation in Korean semis can spill into HK-listed hardware. Keep favoring the internet/consumer HK names (Tencent, Xiaomi) as the core over the higher-beta chip leg, and watch whether the Korean foreign selling is late-stage capitulation (a rebound setup) or the start of a broader EM-Asia de-risking.

items.headline: Hang Seng logs best week since Sep 2025 (+3.7%); Politburo shifts to 'moderately loose,' pledges to boost domestic demand
items.summary: Hong Kong equities posted their best week since September 2025 — the Hang Seng up ~3.7% over five straight winning sessions — after the late-July Politburo shifted its language toward a 'moderately loose' stance and pledged to boost domestic demand in H2. The rally came despite a sub-50 July manufacturing PMI (~49.2) and Q2 GDP at a ~3.5-year low (~4.3%), reflecting a stimulus-hope bid and record southbound inflows over the first seven months of 2026, even as delivery of concrete easing stays incremental (LPR held a 14th month).
items.actionable: A supportive backdrop for the HK-tech core (Tencent, Xiaomi) and the China-inflow trade — the 'moderately loose' pledge and record southbound flows are the bid under the sleeve into Tencent's 12 Aug interim results. But with GDP at a 3.5-yr low and easing still incremental, treat it as a hope trade until delivered; watch whether the Monday/Tuesday HK open carries the momentum.

items.headline: Xiaomi (1810.HK) jumps ~7.7% on two new 'Sky Nomad' EV/SUV models
items.summary: Xiaomi shares rose ~7.7% after Lei Jun teased a 'Sky Nomad' technology launch and the company unveiled two new EV/SUV models (Sky Nomad N90/N70), extending its aggressive electric-vehicle expansion that has been a key second-growth engine alongside its smartphone/IoT core. The move helped power the Hang Seng's strong week and reinforced Xiaomi as a preferred consumer-tech name within the HK core.
items.actionable: A clean company-specific catalyst for the Xiaomi position — the EV ramp is the growth optionality on top of the hardware base. Xiaomi and Tencent remain the preferred internet/consumer HK-tech core over the higher-beta SMIC chip leg; the EV newsflow is a reason to keep the name as a core rather than trade it.

items.headline: Singtel + KKR in advanced talks to buy >80% of ST Telemedia Global Data Centres for >US$3.9B
items.summary: Singtel and KKR are reported to be in advanced talks to take a controlling >80% stake in ST Telemedia Global Data Centres for more than US$3.9B, extending the AI/data-centre capex theme into SGX large-caps. The deal underlines Singtel's pivot toward digital-infrastructure and AI-adjacent assets and lands with the STI at record highs; Singtel has been among the top names for 2026 net retail inflows on the SGX.
items.actionable: A constructive, growth-oriented catalyst for the SGX large-cap sleeve — data-centre/AI-infrastructure exposure via Singtel adds a secular-growth leg to the income-heavy S-REIT/bank book. Positive for the Singtel holding specifically; watch deal confirmation and financing terms.

items.headline: STI at record highs into a heavy SG earnings week — CapLand Ascendas REIT 5 Aug, DBS/SGX 6 Aug, OCBC/UOB 7 Aug
items.summary: The Straits Times Index printed fresh all-time highs (STI +~21% total return YTD), led by the big banks (DBS, OCBC, UOB) and Singtel on wealth-management income and the data-centre theme. A dense earnings week follows: CapitaLand Ascendas REIT reports 5 Aug, DBS/SGX/Venture 6 Aug, and OCBC/UOB 7 Aug. Several houses keep the SG banks Overweight on resilient NIMs and capital returns, while the S-REIT sleeve navigates the higher-for-longer rate backdrop; DBS, Singtel and CapLand Ascendas REIT led 2026 net retail inflows.
items.actionable: A catalyst-heavy week for the SGX banks/REIT sleeve, the owner's largest exposure. The banks are the more insulated (higher-for-longer NIM) leg; the oil de-escalation eases the near-term inflation headwind for the rate-sensitive S-REITs. Watch DBS results 6 Aug and CapLand Ascendas REIT 5 Aug for the read on whether records are earnings-justified before adding.

items.headline: Energy Fuels (UUUU) starts building a commercial-scale HEAVY rare-earth plant at White Mesa; conf call 6 Aug
items.summary: Energy Fuels began constructing a commercial-scale heavy rare-earth (HREE) separation circuit at its White Mesa mill in Utah — a ~US$104M expansion, largely government grant/loan-funded, to co-produce a mixed rare-earth carbonate plus separated oxides (targeting Tb/Dy and other heavies) alongside its already-running NdPr line and uranium. It lands as China's heavy-REE exports remain well below pre-control levels and Western DoD-backed supply builds out; the company hosts a conference call on 6 Aug.
items.actionable: A direct, dated catalyst for the ex-China rare-earth watchlist — heavy REEs (Tb/Dy) are the China chokepoint, so a Western commercial HREE plant is the structural bull case made concrete. Reinforces accumulating government-backed UUUU/MP on weakness into the 10 Nov MOFCOM suspension cliff rather than chasing; watch the 6 Aug call for timeline detail.

items.headline: Lynas (LYC.AX) signs ~US$96M, 4-year Pentagon deal to supply light + heavy rare-earth oxides
items.summary: Lynas Rare Earths signed a roughly US$96M, four-year agreement to supply the US Department of Defense with both light and heavy rare-earth oxides, deepening the Western ex-China supply chain and the government-offtake theme that has re-rated the sector. It follows Lynas's advancing US heavy-REE production (Seadrift/Texas) and sits alongside MP Materials' DoD backing and Energy Fuels' new HREE plant — a coordinated Western build-out against China's ~70% mining / ~90% processing dominance.
items.actionable: Reinforces the ex-China rare-earth thesis with a concrete government offtake — the same DoD-backing dynamic that re-rated MP. Confirms the basket (Lynas, MP, UUUU, USAR) as the Western-supply play into the 10 Nov MOFCOM cliff; accumulate on weakness rather than chase the strategic premium.

items.headline: Amazon AWS +37% blowout; four hyperscalers guide to $720-745B of 2026 capex, re-validating AI spend
items.summary: Amazon rose ~15% (to a record) after AWS grew 37% y/y to $42.2B — its fastest in 18 quarters — with 2026 capex raised to ~$220B; combined with Microsoft, Alphabet and Meta, the four hyperscalers now guide to $720-745B of cumulative 2026 capital spending. That reversed the AI-overcapacity narrative that had wiped >$1trn from semis the prior week, powering the Nasdaq to records into month-end and again on 3 Aug.
items.actionable: The AWS blowout and the $720-745bn hyperscaler capex guide re-validate the AI-infrastructure spend the semis rout had doubted — a positive read-through to the SMIC chip leg and the whole AI-hardware complex. Keep Tencent/Xiaomi favored as the core, but the acute bear case on the chip leg has eased; size the higher-beta chip exposure for two-way volatility.

items.headline: June core PCE cools to 3.3% y/y (from 3.4%); labor data softening keeps the Fed path two-sided
items.summary: The Fed's preferred inflation gauge edged down: June core PCE printed 3.3% y/y (+0.1% m/m) from 3.4%, with headline PCE flat-to-down on the month, while Q2 GDP came in sub-trend (~+1.5% annualized). Alongside a decelerating labor market (sharp downward revisions to prior payroll months in circulation), the data cut against late-July's hawkish rate pricing (which had spiked September-hike odds toward ~80% on the oil spike). The mix — cooling inflation and softening growth — is 'stagflation-lite' but tilts the marginal Fed risk back toward a pause.
items.actionable: Cooling core PCE plus a softer labor tape and the oil crash together relieve some of the higher-for-longer pressure on levered silver and SGX REITs — a modest positive for the rate-sensitive sleeve versus the late-July hawkish scare. But 3.3% core is still well above target, so the Friday 7 Aug July jobs report is the swing input: a weak print revives cut hopes (bullish metals/REITs), a hot one revives the hike risk. Keep the cash pile productive into the print.

items.headline: Crypto stays soft over the weekend: Bitcoin ~$62-63k, sentiment in 'Fear'
items.summary: Crypto lagged the equity records through the weekend after the late-July correction: Bitcoin held around $62-63k (below its 20-day MA), Ether near $1,900-1,950 and Solana in the low-$70s, with the crypto Fear & Greed index in the high-20s ('Fear'). Flows tilted BTC→ETH (spot-Bitcoin ETFs saw weekly outflows while Ether ETFs extended inflows). Crypto's failure to break higher despite equity records flagged that the rate backdrop was still capping risk appetite before Monday's Iran-driven relief.
items.actionable: No direct holding, but crypto is the cleanest read on the risk-appetite impulse — its weekend softness before Monday's rally shows how much of the risk-on turn hangs on the Iran-deal/oil relief rather than a broad easing of financial conditions. Treat it as a barometer: a hot July jobs print (7 Aug) would pressure crypto and the metals/REIT rate-sensitivity trade together; a soft one would relieve both.
